title: Gospel of Thomas, sayings 46-50 (Nag Hammadi Codex II, pages 41-42)
source: Nag Hammadi Codex II page photographs (Claremont Colleges Digital Library, Nag Hammadi Archive) + Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition by Paul Dilley (CC BY 4.0) + English by Mark M. Mattison (public domain)
description: Gospel of Thomas, sayings 46-50, in the Coptic of Nag Hammadi Codex II, pages 41-42, with each saying linked to the photograph of the papyrus page and an English translation.
introduction:
The Gospel of Thomas is a collection of 114 sayings attributed to Jesus, introduced as the hidden sayings written down by Didymos Judas Thomas. The only complete copy is the second tractate of Nag Hammadi Codex II, a papyrus book in Coptic copied in the 4th century and found near Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt in 1945; it is now in the Coptic Museum, Cairo (inv. 10544). Greek fragments of the work survive in three Oxyrhynchus papyri (P. Oxy. 1, 654 and 655), which are not shown here.

This entry covers the sayings 46-50, which begin on codex page 41; the end of saying 50 is on page 42. The Coptic is given line by line; the small numbers are codex page and line (for example 33.5), so each line can be found on the photograph. Page and line breaks follow the Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition by Paul Dilley, which he made from the photographs of The Facsimile Edition of the Nag Hammadi Codices, the negatives shown here.

Photograph: Codex II page 41, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 51, CCDL nha 2885; Nag Hammadi Archive of the Institute for Antiquity and Christianity, Claremont Colleges Digital Library. Checked on the photograph: page 41 line 1 begins 'ⲟⲩⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ ϩⲙⲡⲉϥⲉϩⲟ ⲟⲩⲕⲁ[ⲕⲟ]ⲥ' and line 35 reads 'ϩⲓⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ⳿ ⲟⲩⲁⲁⲧϥ⳿ ⲁϥⲱϩ[ⲉ ⲉⲣⲁⲧϥ]' (the last line breaks off at the lower right).
translator_notes: Coptic: Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition (Paul C. Dilley), version 6.2.0, CC BY 4.0, shown in the manuscript's own spelling with words grouped as bound groups. Editorial signs are the edition's: square brackets mark letters lost in a gap (restored by the editor, or dots for the number of lost letters), a dot under a letter marks an uncertain reading, round brackets write out a letter abbreviated by a stroke at a line end, angle brackets mark letters added by the editor, curly brackets letters the editor removes, double square brackets letters erased by the scribe.

The small numbers in the Coptic are codex page and line (page.line) as marked in the edition. Where a word is divided between two lines on the papyrus, the edition sometimes keeps the word whole on one line, so a line can begin a few letters earlier or later on the photograph (for example 39.33-34, and the page change inside saying 13).

English: Mark M. Mattison, The Gospel of Thomas (public domain). Mattison's symbols: [ ] gap in the text, ( ) editorial insertion, / \ editorial correction of a scribal error. The saying headings are his.
Saying 49: Mattison renders monachos as 'one'; it is usually translated 'single', 'solitary' or 'alone'.

translation.text:
Jesus said, "It's not possible for anyone to mount two horses or stretch two bows, and it's not possible for a servant to follow two leaders, because they'll respect one and despise the other.

"No one drinks old wine and immediately wants to drink new wine. And new wine isn't put in old wineskins, because they'd burst. Nor is old wine put in new wineskins, because it'd spoil.

"A new patch of cloth isn't sewn onto an old coat, because it'd tear apart."
translation.scan_note: On page 41 lines 12-23 (Codex II page 41, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 51, CCDL nha 2885). Opens 'ⲡⲉϫⲉⲓ︤ⲥ︥' at 41.12; ends 'ⲛ̄ϣⲁⲓ ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲡⲱϩ ⲛⲁϣⲱⲡⲉ' at 41.23. 42.7ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲁⲡⲁⲩⲥⲓⲥ
translation.text:
Jesus said, "If they ask you, 'Where do you come from?' tell them, 'We've come from the light, the place where light came into being by itself, [established] itself, and appeared in their image.'

"If they ask you, 'Is it you?' then say, 'We are its children, and we're chosen by our living Father.'

"If they ask you, 'What's the sign of your Father in you?' then say, 'It's movement and rest.'"
translation.scan_note: On page 41 lines 30-35; page 42 lines 1-7 (Codex II page 41, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 51, CCDL nha 2885; Codex II page 42, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 52, CCDL nha 2871). Opens 'ⲡⲉ' at 41.30; ends 'ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲁⲡⲁⲩⲥⲓⲥ' at 42.7. Page and line breaks from the Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition (pb/lb markup); the first and last line of each page were checked on the photograph.
